title: A Global Comparison of Schemas, Transparency, and Interoperability in Public-Sector AI Registers and Inventories
abstract: arXiv:2609.24883v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) registers and inventories aim to make governmental AI visible, but their institutional scope, schemas, and reporting practices construct different representations of public-sector AI. We compare 8,368 records from country-specific and transnational inventories covering 72 countries. Across 23 harmonized fields, registers shared a descriptive core but rarely requested information about appeals, risks, legal bases, or external evaluation. We found that broad schemas often contained substantial missingness, schema similarity showed no significant patterned convergence, and multiple sources covering the same jurisdictions overlapped only selectively. Based on these findings, we synthesize a layered visibility framework that shows how register records reflect disclosure arrangements and why interoperability requires shared concepts, clear definitions, and preserved provenance.

translated_title: 公共部门人工智能登记册与清单的模式、透明度与互操作性全球比较研究
translated_abstract: 人工智能（AI）登记册和清单旨在使政府使用的AI变得可见，但其机构范围、数据模式和报告实践构建了对公共部门AI的不同表征。我们比较了来自覆盖72个国家的国别和跨国清单的8,368条记录。在23个统一字段中，各登记册共享一个描述性核心，但很少要求提供有关申诉、风险、法律依据或外部评估的信息。我们发现，宽泛的数据模式往往包含大量缺失值，模式相似性未显示出显著的规律性趋同，覆盖同一司法辖区的多个数据源之间仅存在选择性重叠。基于这些发现，我们综合提出了一个分层可见性框架，用以说明登记册记录如何反映披露安排，以及为什么互操作性需要共享概念、清晰的定义和保留来源信息。
tldr: 该研究比较了72个国家8,368条公共部门AI登记记录，发现各登记册虽有共同的描述性核心但普遍缺失风险、法律依据等关键信息，并据此提出分层可见性框架，指出实现互操作性需要共享概念、清晰定义和保留数据来源。
en_tdlr: This study compares 8,368 public-sector AI register records across 72 countries, revealing shared descriptive cores but widespread missingness in risks and legal bases, and proposes a layered visibility framework showing that interoperability requires shared concepts, clear definitions, and preserved provenance.
